qs.q: A patient presents with massive haematemesis after prolonged episodes of retching following acute alcohol intoxication. Endoscopy reveals a linear mucosal tear crossing the gastroesophageal junction. What is the most appropriate management approach?
qs.e: Mallory-Weiss tears are superficial mucosal lacerations associated with vomiting that heal rapidly and completely without surgery. Boerhaave syndrome involves transmural tears requiring emergency surgery.

qs.q: A 45-year-old male presents with acute epigastric pain and haematemesis following heavy alcohol and NSAID use. Which histological feature is expected on biopsy?
o: Dominant plasma cells and chronic lymphocytes
Heavy surface epithelial infiltration by eosinophils
Replacement of parietal cells by mucus cells
Mucosal infiltration with neutrophils and oedema
qs.e: Acute gastritis is characterized histologically by mucosal infiltration with neutrophils and oedema, often presenting as erosive and haemorrhagic. Plasma cells and lymphocytes are characteristic of chronic gastritis instead.

qs.q: A patient with advanced alcoholic cirrhosis develops sudden massive haematemesis. Emergency endoscopy reveals ruptured oesophageal varices. What is the mortality rate from this first bleeding episode?
o: Approximately fifty percent despite medical intervention
Approximately ten to fifteen percent even without treatment
Approximately twenty-five to thirty percent with management
Approximately seventy to eighty percent without ligation
qs.e: Approximately 50% of patients die from the first variceal bleeding episode from direct haemorrhage or hepatic coma from the protein load combined with hypovolaemic shock.

qs.q: A 42-year-old male presents after a binge drinking episode with haematemesis. Endoscopy shows linear tears crossing the gastroesophageal junction without perforation into the mediastinum. What distinguishes this from Boerhaave syndrome?
o: Mallory-Weiss requires surgical repair while Boerhaave heals spontaneously
Mallory-Weiss tears occur in the stomach while Boerhaave occurs in the oesophagus
Mallory-Weiss tears are caused by alcohol while Boerhaave is caused by vomiting
Mallory-Weiss tears are superficial while Boerhaave involves transmural perforation
qs.e: Mallory-Weiss tears are superficial mucosal lacerations that heal spontaneously. Boerhaave syndrome involves transmural perforation leading to mediastinitis — a life-threatening surgical emergency.
